lines: Take {gift_item}. I may not have a trade, but I know how to say thanks.
Here, {gift_item}. Maybe one of us will find the perfect use for it.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
You helped the village, and I wanted you to have something for it.
I chose {gift_item} because it looked useful. I hope I guessed right.
No bargain. No favor owed. This is just a gift.
I could have kept {gift_item}, but you will make better use of it.
Please take it before I lose my nerve and overexplain.
I remembered what you did for us. This is my way of saying so.
There is care in this, even if there is no fancy wrapping.
I asked around before choosing {gift_item}. People had opinions.
This felt more honest than another long thank you.
Keep it for the next problem that finds you.
I do not have much to give, but {gift_item} is yours.
You earned more than this, but this is what I can offer today.
I picked something practical because practical things tend to last.
Take {gift_item} and let the thought be enough.
I hope this makes one future day a little easier.
The village remembers who helps it. So do I.
Here. Thanks should not always come with a speech.
Good, {gift_item} worked. See? I can be useful without a workstation.
{tested_villager} liked it? Excellent. I am putting that under possible talents.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}. I like advice that holds up.
Their face changed the moment they saw it. That was a good sign.
I was worried until {tested_villager} smiled.
The gift fit the person instead of just looking impressive.
Remember what worked about {gift_item}. That will help next time.
I am glad we listened before choosing.
That reaction was worth all the second guessing.
A useful gift beats an expensive mistake.
We got it right because we thought about what they needed.
Keep that idea. {tested_villager} clearly approved.
I knew {gift_item} had a chance, but I did not expect it to land that well.
Their thanks sounded honest. You cannot ask for more.
Good advice feels strange. I may try it again.
The choice worked because it suited them.
I noticed they started using it right away.
That is one less awkward gift story for the village.
Next time, trust the same kind of careful guess.
Well done. {gift_item} found the right hands.
Ah. Then my career in advice pauses here. Try {alternative_gift} for {gift_subject}.
{gift_item} was wrong? Let us call it research. {alternative_gift} should work better.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.
We guessed wrong, so let us stop defending the guess.
Set {gift_item} aside. {alternative_gift} deserves a fair try.
I should have asked more about {gift_subject} before choosing.
The silence after that gift told me enough.
A thoughtful gift can still be wrong for the person.
Next time I will listen before I reach for an answer.
I would rather fix the mistake than explain it all evening.
Keep {gift_item} for someone who actually wants it.
Maybe {alternative_gift} will feel less forced.
That choice sounded better in the square than it looked in their hands.
Nobody needs to pretend they liked a poor gift.
We learned something useful, even if we learned it awkwardly.
I will remember that {gift_subject} matters more than the price.
The next gift should suit them, not our pride.
Let us ask one good question before trying again.
I noticed the disappointment before anyone spoke.
Fine. My advice missed. We can make a better choice now.
This is why nobody pays me for advice. Try {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess. {alternative_gift} next time.
I knew I should have kept that guess to myself.
Try {alternative_gift}. I trust that choice more than the last one.
Put {gift_item} away before this gets any more awkward.
I would rather hear the truth than watch someone fake a smile.
Next time I am asking twice before I recommend anything.
That poor gift is going to follow me around the square all week.
Maybe they needed something simpler from the start.
I am not blaming them. I would not want the <shake>wrong</shake> gift either.
Let us give this another try after everyone calms down.
{alternative_gift} at least sounds like it belongs in the same conversation.
I should have paid attention to the hesitation.
A bad guess does not improve because we meant well.
I will keep my next bit of advice shorter and safer.
No more surprises until we actually know what they like.
I can admit when I made the wrong call. This was one.
Please do not tell the whole square how confidently I suggested {gift_item}.
We can recover from an awkward gift. We just need a better one.
You came back? Fair. My next guess is {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess. {alternative_gift} next time.
You asked for my guess, and now we both know it was a bad one.
Do not wave {gift_item} at them again. Bring {alternative_gift}.
Their face answered before their mouth did.
Fine. Next time we choose with our eyes open.
I am not going to argue someone into liking a gift.
A poor choice stays poor no matter how nicely you wrap it.
Try listening to them instead of guessing louder.
Set {gift_item} down and stop making this worse.
{alternative_gift} has a better chance, which is not saying much.
We embarrassed ourselves once. That is enough practice.
If they dislike it, believe them the first time.
I can take the blame for the advice. You can take the hint.
The village has enough gossip without another failed gift.
Choose something useful, not something that makes you look clever.
I will not defend {gift_item} just because it was my idea.
Bring {alternative_gift} and keep the speech short.
<shake>Wrong</shake> gift, wrong moment, bad guess. Let us move on.
